text.arabic_uthmani: فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًۭا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًۭا

baseline.text: Orada kullarımızdan bir kul buldular. Ona katımızdan rahmet vermiş ve kendisine tarafımızdan bir bilgi öğretmiştik.

findings.text: Adamın önce kul oluşuyla tanımlanması, aldığı merhamet ve bilgiyi kendi egemenliği saymadan eyleme aktardığını gösterir; yetkisi bağımlı ve verilmiştir.
Bilginin Allah katından gelmesi, onun kaynağını uzak bir soyutlama değil, eylemi yöneten yakın bir sınır olarak kurar.

activation_trace.role: Obedient, humbled service supplies the recipient's governing relation rather than merely a social label.
Giving supplies the transfer of mercy and marks it as an endowment.
Near presence gives the source phrase a proximate, present-at-hand force.
Disclosure to a knower supplies the taught capacity and keeps it received.

changed_reading.after: They find an obediently commissioned recipient whose mercy and knowledge remain gifts from a near divine source.
changed_reading.before: They encounter a knowledgeable holy man.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عَبْدًا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَا together with the two first-person-plural grant and source clauses.
baseline_models.mechanism: The doubled servant root places the person inside obedient belonging, while mercy and knowledge are received capacities whose source remains near rather than self-generated.

activation_trace.role: Bestowal supplies the common received status of the first capacity.
Tender beneficence supplies the relational and protective pole of the pair.
Cognitive disclosure supplies the discerning pole coordinated with mercy.

changed_reading.after: Mercy and knowledge stand together as paired equipment: beneficent responsiveness is joined to disclosed understanding.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is one honor and knowledge another.

baseline_models.mechanism: Two coordinated transitive clauses pair beneficent responsiveness with disclosed understanding; the focus presents them as a coupled profile rather than unrelated honors.

activation_trace.role: Coming upon the sought object supplies the encounter as discovery.
A distinguishing sign that guides supplies the servant's possible function as a human marker.

changed_reading.after: The encounter itself is a marked discovery, with the servant functioning as a signpost at the route's decisive transition.
changed_reading.before: The servant is an incidental person met on the route.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَوَجَدَا joined in the focus sentence to وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Finding is coupled to a root whose inventory includes both knowing and a distinguishing mark, allowing the servant to function as a discovered locus that marks the sought transition.

activation_trace.role: Finding the sought object anchors the recovered route in the focus encounter.
Loss of active remembrance supplies the failure that hides the sought point.
Return to a prior location reverses linear progress and enables recovery.
Going behind a prior trace supplies the residual track used as guide.
Following an أثر step by step turns reversal into exact retracing.

changed_reading.after: They find him when failed attention is repaired and the route is read backward through residual signs.
changed_reading.before: They find him after persistent forward travel.

context_deltas.mechanism: The encounter becomes the endpoint of repaired attention: a missed sign permits overshoot, remembered anomaly causes reversal, and residual traces guide the pair back to the person.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies arrival, forgetting, overshoot, remembrance, and retracing; I supply the arrow that repaired attention to the sign enables the finding. Alternatively, the sequence may describe route recovery without characterizing the encounter itself.
structural_cues: The sequence reaches the meeting point in 18:61, passes it in 18:62, remembers the anomalous sign in 18:63, and retraces in 18:64 immediately before the focus.

activation_trace.role: Disclosed knowledge anchors the teaching process in the focus endowment.
Tracing step after step supplies learning by sequenced accompaniment.
Sound handling of an affair defines the requested learning as practical discernment.
Incomplete encompassing knowledge supplies the learner's inability to hold the whole event.
Knowledge of a report and its interior supplies the missing depth behind the visible act.
Newly produced speech or news makes explanation teacher-timed and event-linked.
A reminder supplies the later disclosure that permits the event to be reread.

changed_reading.after: The focus knowledge is enacted under asymmetry: follow first, suspend surface judgment, then receive the interior account after the event.
changed_reading.before: The focus knowledge is a stock of propositions that can be transferred in advance.

context_deltas.mechanism: Knowledge is transmitted through sequenced accompaniment: the learner follows before understanding, lacks the event's interior, and receives an explanatory reminder only after the experience has unfolded.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies following, requested teaching, missing interior knowledge, and delayed mention; I infer an experience-first pedagogy in which suspension preserves teachability. Alternatively, delayed explanation may be only a discipline of companionship, not a general teaching method.
structural_cues: The learner asks to follow in order to be taught in 18:66, while 18:70 defers questions until the teacher initiates an account.

activation_trace.role: Obedient service supplies the human agent's subordinate relation.
Near-source presence anchors the capacities outside autonomous possession.
Lordly cultivation and completion supplies the commissioning source behind the mercy.
The servant's explicit doing names execution at the human level.
Command, negated as his own, marks the upper boundary on that execution.

changed_reading.after: His exceptionality is commissioned and bounded: he receives, enacts, and explains, but does not claim originary ownership of gift or act.
changed_reading.before: The specially taught servant exercises an exceptional personal authority.

context_deltas.mechanism: The source clauses in the focus and the closing denial of self-origin place the servant between reception and execution: he acts, but neither gift nor commission is authored by him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies externally sourced gifts, explicit human action, and denial of self-origin; I infer a recipient-executor rather than an autonomous author. Alternatively, the denial may delimit only the three narrated acts, not every exercise of his knowledge.
structural_cues: 18:65 repeats first-person-plural possession and source phrases; 18:82 closes by denying that the actions arose from the servant's own command or affair.

activation_trace.role: Tender beneficence anchors preservation as mercy rather than arbitrary damage.
Disclosed understanding supplies awareness of the threat hidden from the immediate scene.
A literal split or hole supplies the limited defect placed in the vessel.
Seizing and taking supplies the ruler's appropriation mechanism.
Wrongful coercive taking supplies the larger loss that the small defect blocks.

changed_reading.after: Mercy informed by hidden knowledge may preserve the whole through a calibrated defect that looks harmful at the surface.
changed_reading.before: Mercy should appear as immediate repair, intactness, or relief.

context_deltas.mechanism: A bounded breach lowers the vessel's fitness for coercive seizure, so the mercy-knowledge pair preserves the working possession by accepting visible local damage.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the breach and the coercive seizure; I infer that the defect makes the vessel unfit enough to escape taking. The live alternative is that the packet leaves the king's exact selection rule unstated.
structural_cues: The vessel breached in 18:71 is identified again in 18:79 as a livelihood exposed to a king's forcible seizure; the explanation is delayed until after separation.

activation_trace.role: A protected generative enclosure supplies the material analogy of mercy holding value until readiness.
The raised wall supplies the physical barrier repaired before collapse.
Separation from a guardian supplies beneficiaries not yet able to secure the reserve.
Stored wealth supplies the provision held out of immediate reach.
Attaining full strength supplies the release condition.
Bringing something out of concealment supplies eventual delivery.
The packet's explicit tender beneficence names the timed preservation as mercy.

changed_reading.after: Mercy can guard a hidden grant by delaying access until the recipient has matured into capacity.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is an immediately accessible compassionate benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repair turns the wall into temporal custody: stored value remains enclosed while orphaned owners mature, then exits concealment; mercy thus operates as timing architecture as well as tenderness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies barrier, treasure, orphanhood, maturity, extraction, and mercy; I infer the wall as a timed container and use the womb branch as a material analogy. Alternatively, the mechanism is ordinary guardianship and economic preservation without gestational force.
structural_cues: 18:77 repairs a wall without wage; 18:82 links that repair to orphans, hidden treasure, maturity, extraction, and explicitly to mercy.

remaining_uncertainties: The focus syntax pairs mercy and knowledge but does not state whether mercy causes, governs, or merely accompanies knowledge.
The vessel's exemption mechanism is inferred; the packet names coercive seizure but not the king's exact selection rule.
The womb and water readings are deliberately branch-distant material analogies.
The boy and replacement sequence remains ethically and causally underdetermined from the packet and is not promoted to a stable model.
strongest_changes: Finding is recast as recovery through a missed sign and exact retracing.
Knowledge becomes delayed experiential disclosure joined to mercy and bounded by commissioned agency.
Mercy can preserve through calibrated defect or delayed access rather than immediate surface benefit.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's dense repetition of servant, source, gift, and teaching became operational when the surrounding sequence supplied missed signs, asymmetric accompaniment, delayed explanations, and three interventions whose visible forms diverge from their later purposes.

activation_trace.role: A channel that routes water supplies a flow-form for the bestowed mercy.
Abundant gathered water supplies a reservoir image for the taught knowledge.
Joining separated elements supplies the confluence where the routed gift is sought.
Vast abundant water supplies the material field surrounding the encounter.
Water's seepage and flow supplies the anomalous path that points toward discovery.

changed_reading.after: The mercy-bearing gift and knowledge can be imagined as a routed influx from beyond the local site, discovered where flows and paths meet.
changed_reading.before: Mercy and knowledge are static deposits possessed by the servant.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it materializes abstract gifts as water infrastructure; it remains anchored because the focus branches explicitly supply channel and abundant-water images and the approach supplies confluence and water-trace cues. Render only as an exploratory material analogy, never as a lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ءَاتَيْنَاهُ and عِلْمًا through the focus branches for routed water and gathered abundance.

activation_trace.role: Coming upon the sought person supplies the first finding in the reciprocal sequence.
Capacity and sufficiency let 'you will find me patient' turn finding into an audit of learner capacity.
Coming upon the wall shifts discovery from a person to an object carrying a latent condition.
Unmaking a built structure supplies the wall's hidden collapse trajectory.

changed_reading.after: The focus opens a chain of findings that tests capacities and detects latent trajectories: they find him, he is to find their patience, and they find what is about to fail.
changed_reading.before: Finding the servant is a one-way act of locating a person.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it treats a repeated ordinary verb as a reciprocal diagnostic frame; it remains valid because the exact focus root recurs when patience is to be found and when a wall with a latent trajectory is found. Render as a discourse-pattern possibility, not a claim that all three findings are semantically identical.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَوَجَدَا in 18:65, echoed by the finding promise in 18:69 and the dual finding in 18:77.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Servanthood coordinates received mercy and received knowledge.** `ع ب د` B003 (“worship and submissive obedience”) identifies the man by relation before gifts are named; `ع ل م` B001 then marks knowledge as taught from God. Later he denies acting from his own command (18:82). I infer that submissive agency is what transmits hidden knowledge into action without claiming ownership. His authority is derivative, not autonomous expertise.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:82 confirmed that the servant’s knowledge and acts remain derivative from a command not his own.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Knowledge sourced at a proximal boundary.** `ل د ن/B002` is a proximal starting boundary in place or time. The doubled source constructions `مِنْ عِندِنَا` and `مِن لَّدُنَّا` place mercy and knowledge near their giver; 18:66 asks for transmitted instruction, while 18:67–70 imposes conditions on how that knowledge can be approached. I infer that proximity of source does not eliminate pedagogical distance for the learner. `مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًا` reads as source-qualified knowledge whose effects cannot be inferred merely from visible sequence.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:66–70 unexpectedly showed that source-near knowledge still requires mediated teaching, restraint, agreement, and controlled disclosure.

words.gloss_range: resultative sequential particle; no lexical root range
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) opens the verse as a tight consequence from the return in 18:64. Because it is fused into {{ar:وَجَدَا}} ({{tr:wajadā}}), the discovery reads as the immediate landing of the retracing, not as a fresh scene with narrative space in between.

topics.headline: immediate result-scene opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the encounter is the immediate harvest of the return in 18:64, not a detached new episode.
topics.reason: The rows cohere with QAC fāʾ al-taʿqīb and the clause boundary: the particle opens 18:65 as direct sequence and consequence from 18:64.

topics.headline: proclitic liaison into finding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the connector fused to the finding verb, so the narrative does not restart before the discovery.
topics.reason: The written and recited attachment of the particle to the following verb supports a compact transition into the act of finding.

words.gloss_range: completed finding or encounter after search, with broader felt-possession pressure narrowed to this local discovery
words.prose: {{ar:وَجَدَا}} ({{tr:wajadā}}) is a perfect dual verb, so the two travelers from 18:64 arrive together at a completed finding. Its direct object is {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}), which narrows the broad w-j-d pressure of finding, felt possession, and encounter into a searched-for personal encounter. The same root also opens a Surah 18 finding thread that later turns discoveries into disclosures (18:77; 18:86), and the long final ā of {{ar:وَجَدَا}} ({{tr:wajadā}}) is later answered by the -nāhu cadence of the two divine actions.
words.root_gloss_range: finding, encountering, experiencing, and possessing; local Form I perfect selects completed discovery by the two travelers

topics.headline: completed dual discovery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the same two returners from 18:64 as the joint subjects of a completed discovery.
topics.reason: Perfect dual morphology and attachment evidence keep the action completed and performed by the same pair.

topics.headline: search becomes personal encounter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the search resolves into encountering a person as direct object, not merely reaching a place or sign.
topics.reason: The w-j-d range includes felt possession and inward experience, but local syntax narrows it to completed encounter with {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}) as object.

topics.headline: Surah 18 finding thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track finding as a Surah 18 narrative signal whose later instances disclose hidden conditions (18:77; 18:86).
topics.reason: Concrete same-surah references support a recurrence pattern without controlling the local parse.

topics.headline: long-vowel cadence into divine actions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening long-vowel cadence later answered by the two divine action forms.
topics.reason: The phonetic row offers a real local sound link, though it remains secondary to syntax and meaning.

words.gloss_range: a singular indefinite servant, locally specified as one from the divine servant-class
words.prose: {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}) is the accusative object found by the two travelers, then the same servant is carried forward by the -hu suffixes in the giving and teaching clauses. Its indefinite singular form introduces him without a name, but {{ar:مِنْ عِبَادِنَا}} ({{tr:min ʿibādinā}}) immediately places him within a divine servant-class. The ʿ-b-d pressure of dependence, service, and devotion matters because mercy and knowledge are attached to someone first profiled as a servant, and the shared -an cadence of {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}), {{ar:رَحْمَةً}} ({{tr:raḥmatan}}), and {{ar:عِلْمًا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}) makes that profile audible as a unit.
words.root_gloss_range: serving, worship, devotion, and owned dependence; local noun foregrounds servanthood before personal identity

topics.headline: found object becomes endowed recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the found object become the same recipient in both later divine clauses.
topics.reason: Accusative object status and the later -hu suffixes keep one servant continuous across finding, giving, and teaching.

topics.headline: unnamed singular within a divine class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a paradoxical introduction: one unnamed servant is immediately made specific by belonging to Our servants.
topics.reason: The indefinite singular and the following partitive phrase jointly support anonymity without vagueness.

topics.headline: dependence and devotion before title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the extraordinary figure is first defined by dependence and devotion, not by a personal name or formal title.
topics.reason: The ʿ-b-d range supports service, worship, dependence, and devotion; local grammar keeps those pressures within the servant identity rather than turning them into a separate title claim.

topics.headline: servant, mercy, and knowledge profile
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the servant and the two endowed contents as one profile rather than separate details.
topics.reason: The shared accusative tanwīn and the rare servant-plus-mercy-plus-knowledge profile support a local three-part unit.

words.gloss_range: partitive and specifying preposition in the servant-class phrase
words.prose: The first {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is partitive: the found servant is from among {{ar:عِبَادِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿibādinā}}). It also starts the ayah's repeated min architecture, which moves from belonging to the divine servant-class, then to the source of mercy, then to the inner source of knowledge.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Our servants as the class phrase

topics.headline: from among Our servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition selects the servant from within the class and specifies what kind of servant he is.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify this min as partitive, with a specifying force that qualifies the indefinite servant.

topics.headline: first step in the three-min architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the first min begin the verse-wide movement from class source to mercy source to knowledge source.
topics.reason: The row is structurally coherent with the three occurrences of min in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: genitive plural servant-class with first-person plural possessive suffix
words.prose: {{ar:عِبَادِنَآ}} ({{tr:ʿibādinā}}) is the genitive plural class governed by the first {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}). The -nā suffix makes the class definite by divine possession, while the plural embeds the singular {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}) inside a larger field of God's servants. That servant-class is the field in which the later mercy and knowledge gifts become intelligible, and the word begins a repeated -nā cadence that keeps divine possession, agency, and sourcehood audible through the verse.
words.root_gloss_range: servants, worshipers, and devotees in divine possession; local plural construct marks a dignified class belonging to Us

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition in the repeated min architecture

topics.headline: divinely possessed plural class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the class is plural, definite by possession, and governed by min as the source-set for the singular servant.
topics.reason: The genitive plural, construct relation, and -nā suffix are all locally licensed and define the servant-class.

topics.headline: servanthood tied to mercy and knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the servant-class as the field in which the later mercy and knowledge gifts become intelligible.
topics.reason: Same-surah and co-occurrence rows support a servant vocabulary thread that remains subordinate to the local phrase.

topics.headline: singular servant embedded in plural servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local root echo from one servant to Our servants, making uniqueness a form of belonging.
topics.reason: The short-range repetition of the ʿ-b-d root and the singular-to-plural movement are direct local evidence.

topics.headline: first -nā cadence of divine possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine possession begin a repeated -nā cadence that will return in the source and action words.
topics.reason: The sound row is locally grounded in repeated -nā forms across the verse.

words.gloss_range: Form IV bestowal: We gave him, with -hu as recipient and mercy as gift
words.prose: {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}) is Form IV: the root's coming-pressure is narrowed into causative bestowal, so mercy is caused to come to the servant. The -hu suffix makes him the recipient, and {{ar:رَحْمَةً}} ({{tr:raḥmatan}}) names the gift. The wording also recalls the request for mercy in 18:10 and turns petition-language into a completed grant here, while the -nāhu cadence pairs {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}) with {{ar:عَلَّمْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ʿallamnāhu}}) before their different gifts are parsed.
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arrival, and causing to come; local Form IV selects causative giving or bestowal

topics.headline: giver, recipient, and mercy compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the servant is grammatically made recipient before mercy is named as the transferred gift.
topics.reason: The double-object grammar and perfect Form IV directly support completed bestowal from divine subject to servant recipient.

topics.headline: request in 18:10 becomes grant in 18:65
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the cave prayer for mercy (18:10) reappear as mercy already bestowed on the servant in 18:65.
topics.reason: The concrete same-surah recurrence of the ʾ-t-y plus mercy field supports an echo from petition to fulfilled grant.

topics.headline: paired -nāhu divine actions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}) paired with {{ar:عَلَّمْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ʿallamnāhu}}) before parsing the distinct gifts.
topics.reason: The shared -nāhu form and parallel double-object construction support the pairing.

words.gloss_range: a particular bestowed mercy, sourced from divine nearness and paired with knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:رَحْمَةًۭ}} ({{tr:raḥmatan}}) is an accusative indefinite verbal noun, the actual gift given by {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}). Its r-ḥ-m background gives the mercy a nurturing-care pressure, while the form keeps it particular rather than totalized. The word also links the servant to Surah 18's mercy thread and to the mercy-knowledge pairing in 40:7, and its -an sound joins {{ar:عَبْدًا}} ({{tr:ʿabdan}}) and {{ar:عِلْمًا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}) in one audible profile.
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, compassion, tenderness, and womb-like care; local accusative maṣdar is the gift given

topics.headline: particular mercy as given object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices mercy as a specific bestowed content, not the total divine attribute or a loose mood.
topics.reason: The accusative indefinite verbal noun functions as the explicit object of the giving verb.

topics.headline: womb-tenderness as mercy pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the first gift as sustaining, nurturing care before the knowledge clause arrives.
topics.reason: The r-ḥ-m family supports womb and tenderness imagery; local grammar narrows this to semantic pressure on mercy, not a separate literal image.

topics.headline: mercy thread and mercy-knowledge pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes mercy as part of a Surah 18 thread and a wider mercy-knowledge pairing (40:7).
topics.reason: The cited references support mercy recurring from 18:10 through 18:82 and pairing with knowledge in 40:7.

topics.headline: accusative -an chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears servant, mercy, and knowledge bound by the same indefinite accusative cadence.
topics.reason: The sound row is directly grounded in the three -an nouns of the ayah.

words.gloss_range: source preposition for the mercy clause
words.prose: The second {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) changes the repeated particle from membership to source. It routes {{ar:رَحْمَةً}} ({{tr:raḥmatan}}) from {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}), completing the mercy channel before the coordinated knowledge channel begins. Its nasal closure also binds into {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}), so the sound surface reinforces the governed source phrase.

topics.headline: source of the mercy channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is not merely possessed by the servant; its origin is routed from divine presence.
topics.reason: The preposition before {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) is locally licensed as source and may qualify both the giving and the gift.

topics.headline: parallel source channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the mercy source here with the knowledge source later rather than treating both min phrases as identical.
topics.reason: The row is supported by the later matching min plus proximity term in the knowledge clause.

topics.headline: nasal binding into source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the preposition cling to the source phrase it governs.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is locally bounded and does not add a separate semantic claim.

words.gloss_range: with Us, from Our presence; local source of mercy in manifest divine nearness
words.prose: {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) closes the first bestowal as a governed source phrase: mercy is from Our presence. The -nā suffix makes the source explicitly divine, while the contrast with {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}) later lets this word carry manifest-nearness force rather than the deeper inner-source force of the knowledge clause. It also joins Surah 18's divine-side valuation language (18:46) and the repeated -nā source cadence.
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, presence, possession, and repository; local form selects divine-side source, not deviation

topics.headline: defined divine source for mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first gift closes on a definite divine locus, not on mercy alone.
topics.reason: Min-governance, locative adverb form, and the -nā suffix make the phrase a defined source for the first bestowal.

topics.headline: manifest nearness contrasted with inner nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the manifest source of mercy from the deeper inner source of knowledge later in the verse.
topics.reason: The local contrast with {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}) supports exterior or manifest proximity; the deviation branch of the root is blocked by context.

topics.headline: divine-side valuation and repository field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase as part of Quranic and Surah 18 language for what is with the divine side (18:46).
topics.reason: The concrete same-surah reference and broader repository formulas support a background field without replacing the local mercy-source reading.

topics.headline: -nā source cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this source term join the repeated -nā chain of divine possession and sourcehood.
topics.reason: The row is a local cadence observation tied to repeated suffix forms.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining two complete divine bestowal clauses
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa-}}) coordinates the second divine action with the first. It keeps {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}) and {{ar:عَلَّمْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ʿallamnāhu}}) paired but distinct: mercy is given, and knowledge is taught. The light connector then flows into the geminated teaching verb, so the sound turn matches the move from conjunction into weighty instruction.

topics.headline: coordination without collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy-giving and knowledge-teaching stand side by side as paired but distinct divine actions.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses coordination from the giving verb to the teaching verb, preserving equality and distinction.

topics.headline: light connector into heavy teaching verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the light coordinator turn into the heavier geminated teaching action.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is locally grounded in the attached wa plus following Form II verb.

words.gloss_range: Form II divine teaching: We taught him, with -hu as recipient and knowledge as taught content
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَّمْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ʿallamnāhu}}) repeats the divine-subject plus servant-object pattern of {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}), but the Form II stem changes the transfer mode: knowledge is caused to be known through deliberate teaching. The ʿ-l-m field also gives the servant a marked-by-knowledge pressure, while the local grammar keeps teaching as the selected sense. This verb prepares the request to learn in 18:66.
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, teaching, marking, and making known; local Form II selects deliberate causative instruction

topics.headline: deliberate divine teaching, not mere notice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices knowledge as something God actively makes the servant know, not as a vague possession.
topics.reason: Form II, double transitivity, perfect aspect, and the explicit knowledge object all support deliberate causative teaching.

topics.headline: teaching also marks the servant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the servant as made recognizable by taught knowledge, while local syntax keeps teaching as the selected action.
topics.reason: The marking branch belongs to the ʿ-l-m family and remains as semantic pressure, but the local Form II verb selects teaching rather than literal branding.

topics.headline: divine teaching opens the learning scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the next ayah’s request to learn (18:66) as dependent on the divine teaching stated here.
topics.reason: Nearby 18:66 and the repeated ʿ-l-m root make the forward bridge concrete.

topics.headline: parallel verbs, pronouns, and source contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks a balanced architecture: same divine subject and servant object, but different transfer modes, objects, and source depths.
topics.reason: The shared -nāhu pattern, wa-coordination, and different source phrases support the architecture.

words.gloss_range: source preposition for the knowledge clause
words.prose: The third {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) places the source phrase before the final object {{ar:عِلْمًا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}). It completes the min progression from class membership to mercy source to knowledge source, so the closing knowledge is heard as inner-sourced before it is named. Its nasal sound binds into {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}), and the source-qualified knowledge becomes the first content of the new servant story opened after the retracing of 18:64.

topics.headline: source route into final knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reaches the final knowledge object through its source first, so sourcehood shapes the closure before the noun lands.
topics.reason: The preposition before {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}) is locally licensed as source for both the teaching act and the knowledge taught.

topics.headline: nasal binding into inner-source term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears min fuse into the doubled-nūn source term that follows.
topics.reason: The sound row is a local phonetic support for attachment to the following source term.

topics.headline: source-qualified knowledge opens the servant story
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the retracing of 18:64 become entry into a new story whose first content is source-qualified knowledge.
topics.reason: The boundary row links the previous trace-following to the servant narrative without changing the local prepositional grammar.

words.gloss_range: from Our intimate inner nearness; governed source for the taught knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}) is governed by the third {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) as the source of the taught knowledge. It is more intimate and interior than {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}), so mercy and knowledge are not sourced through identical proximity terms; the ladun family also adds a direct, pliant pressure without replacing sourcehood. The assimilated form keeps ladun plus -nā visible, echoes the cave prayer's nearness term with a new object (18:10), and its position immediately before {{ar:عِلْمًا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}) makes the final word land as inner-sourced knowledge.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition in the repeated min architecture

topics.headline: point-of-contact inner source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes knowledge as coming from intimate inner nearness, deeper than the manifest source of mercy.
topics.reason: Min-governance and the contrast with {{ar:عِنْدِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) support inner-source proximity for knowledge.

topics.headline: direct and pliant source pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense a pliant, immediate quality in the source term, while the main local force remains sourcehood from divine nearness.
topics.reason: The supplied family evidence supports this as root-image pressure only; it does not replace the governed source function.

topics.headline: ladun plus -nā made audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the fused form as both intimate source term and explicitly divine suffix.
topics.reason: The qiraat rows expose ladun plus -nā while confirming that the source meaning survives nūn simplification.

topics.headline: ladun request re-voiced in 18:65
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the nearness term from the cave prayer (18:10) return with a new object: knowledge rather than mercy.
topics.reason: The concrete 18:10 recurrence supports an echo while the local clause controls the object as knowledge.

topics.headline: penultimate source shapes final word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reaches the ayah’s last word already marked by divine inner source and unframed divine speech.
topics.reason: The source term immediately precedes {{ar:عِلْمًا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}) and participates in the unframed first-person divine characterization.

words.gloss_range: a bounded taught knowledge, final object of the teaching clause and closure of the ayah
words.prose: {{ar:عِلْمًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿilman}}) is the final accusative maṣdar and the named content of {{ar:عَلَّمْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ʿallamnāhu}}). Its indefiniteness makes the knowledge specific and bounded rather than totalized, while the ʿ-l-m field gives it the pressure of certain, marked, sign-reading cognition. As the last word, it completes the servant's mercy-knowledge profile and becomes the basis for the learning request in 18:66.
words.root_gloss_range: knowledge, certain cognition, signs, marking, and teaching; local maṣdar is specific taught content, not unrestricted omniscience

topics.headline: specific taught knowledge, not totalized knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final knowledge as a specific endowed content, not unrestricted omniscience.
topics.reason: Indefinite accusative maṣdar form and object status support bounded taught content from {{ar:لَدُنَّا}} ({{tr:ladunnā}}).

topics.headline: certain knowledge as sign-reading capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the knowledge as certain, marked cognition that can read signs, not bare stored data.
topics.reason: The ʿ-l-m family supports signs, marks, and certainty; local syntax narrows it to the taught content and knowing-state of the servant.

topics.headline: mercy and knowledge complete the servant profile
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes knowledge as the second defining endowment paired with mercy and servanthood, including the mercy-knowledge parallel in 40:7.
topics.reason: The local double-object grammar and the 40:7 parallel support a profile in which mercy and knowledge belong together.

topics.headline: final landing and next-scene pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah land on knowledge and then feel that knowledge become the object of pursuit in 18:66.
topics.reason: Closure position, root echo with the teaching verb, and the next ayah’s learning request support the forward pressure.
